status.en: 85 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Islamabad, Kabul and Peshawar.
status.nb: 85 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Islamabad, Kabul og Peshawar.

summary.en: Recent incidents show continued violence in Pakistan and Afghanistan, with a passenger coach and LPG bowser collision killing ten people on the Makran coastal highway near Ormara, and a roadside blast killing two civilians in Zhob. The Pakistani security forces arrested a suspected TTP terrorist in Karachi's Manghopir and a policeman was killed in Bannu, while a high-voltage cable fell on a house in Turbat, killing a woman. In Afghanistan, Taliban forces demolished a mosque entrance in Maidan Wardak, and Russia expanded diplomatic contacts with the Taliban-led government. A Pakistani bank’s exit has cut a vital lifeline for Afghanistan’s banking sector, and a Russian military aircraft crash killed nineteen people. The conflict recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Nylige hendelser viser fortsatt vold i Pakistan og Afghanistan, med en kollisjon mellom en passasjerbuss og en LPG-bøtte som drepte ti personer på Makran-kystveien nær Ormara, og en veibombe som drepte to sivile i Zhob. Pakistanske sikkerhetsstyrker arresterte en mistenkt TTP-terrorist i Manghopir i Karachi, og en politimann ble drept i Bannu, mens en høyspenningskabel falt på et hus i Turbat og drepte en kvinne. I Afghanistan rev Taliban-styrker ned en moskéinngang i Maidan Wardak, og Russland utvidet diplomatiske kontakter med den Taliban-ledede regjeringen. En pakistansk banks uttreden har kuttet en viktig livslinje for Afghanistans banksystem, og et russisk militærfly styrtet og drepte nitten personer. Konflikten registrerte 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
